title: Remainder boxes: Proof strip
summary: Assign each reading x to box ((x % 5) + 5) % 5. Produce the five box counts in box order 0 through 4. Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.
descriptionMd:
Five pigeonholes collect signed correction slips according to their normalized remainder. Ivo rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

Assign each reading x to box ((x % 5) + 5) % 5. Produce the five box counts in box order 0 through 4.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement remainderBoxesProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Map grouping. Assign each reading x to box ((x % 5) + 5) % 5. Produce the five box counts in box order 0 through 4. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.

referenceSolutions.python:
def remainderBoxesProofStrip(readings, k):
    a=readings
    out=[]
    out=[0]*5
    for x in a: out[x%5]+=1
    return out
